questions.q: More verbs with he / she / it
questions.e: Add -s or -es. Verbs ending in consonant + y change y to -ies.

questions.q: My uncle never ___ coffee.
questions.e: With he / she / it (my uncle) the present simple verb takes -s: drinks.

questions.s: My brother plays chess on Fridays.
questions.fa: Say what your brother does on Fridays.
questions.e: With he / she / it the present simple verb takes -s: plays.

questions.s: They do not eat meat.
questions.fa: Say they do not eat meat.
questions.e: Negative: do not + base verb.

questions.s: What time does the film start?
questions.fa: Ask about the starting time of the film.
questions.e: Question: question word + does + subject + base verb.

questions.s: We usually go to bed at ten.
questions.fa: Say what time you usually go to bed.
questions.e: With we the verb has no -s. Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb.

questions.s: Does your sister speak French?
questions.fa: Ask if someone's sister speaks French.
questions.e: After Does the verb stays in the base form.

questions.s: The sun rises in the east.
questions.fa: Say a fact about the sun.
questions.e: A general fact → present simple. With it / the sun the verb takes -s.

questions.s: My mother work in a hospital.
questions.e: With he / she / it (my mother) the verb takes -s.

questions.s: Do she like tea?
questions.e: With he / she / it the question starts with Does.

questions.s: They doesn't live in Tehran.
questions.e: With they the negative is don't, not doesn't.

questions.s: He watch TV every evening.
questions.e: With he the verb takes -es: watches.

questions.s: What time do the shop open?
questions.e: With the shop (it) we use does.

questions.s: I likes pizza very much.
questions.e: With I the verb has no -s.

questions.q: He always ___ (drink) tea in the morning.
questions.e: With he the present simple verb takes -s: drinks.

questions.q: My parents ___ (not / like) loud music.
questions.e: With they the negative is don't + base verb.

questions.q: She ___ (go) to the gym on Mondays.
questions.e: Verbs ending in -o take -es: goes.

questions.q: ___ (do) your brother play tennis?
questions.e: With he / she / it the question starts with Does.

questions.q: The bus ___ (leave) at 8.15 every morning.
questions.e: A regular timetable → present simple. With it the verb takes -s.

questions.q: Tom ___ (not / eat) breakfast at home.
questions.e: With he the negative is doesn't + base verb.

questions.q: My dog ___ (have) a long tail.
questions.e: With he / she / it, have becomes has.

questions.q: She ___ to school every day.
questions.e: For he / she / it in the present simple, add -s or -es to the verb: She goes.

questions.q: We usually ___ TV in the evening.
questions.e: The adverb usually shows a habit → present simple. With we, the verb has no -s.

questions.q: ___ you like pizza?
questions.e: Present simple questions with I / you / we / they start with Do.

questions.q: My brother ___ get up early on Sundays.
questions.e: With he / she / it the negative is doesn't + base verb.

questions.s: My father works in a bank.
questions.fa: Say where my father works.
questions.e: Third person singular → the verb takes -s: works.

questions.s: Does she play the piano?
questions.fa: Ask if she plays the piano.
questions.e: Questions: Does + subject + base verb.

questions.s: He don't like cold milk.
questions.e: With He (third person singular) the negative auxiliary is doesn't, not don't.

questions.s: She go to work by bus.
questions.e: With she / he / it the verb takes -s or -es: goes.

questions.q: My sister ___ (watch) cartoons every day.
questions.e: Verbs ending in -ch take -es: watches.

questions.q: Water ___ (boil) at 100 degrees.
questions.e: Facts use the present simple; with it the verb takes -s: boils.

questions.q: Verbs with he / she / it
questions.e: Add -s or -es. Verbs ending in consonant + y change y to -ies; have becomes has.

questions.q: Where ___ your cousin live?
questions.e: Wh- questions in the present simple use do / does. With he / she / it we use does.

questions.q: Who ___ the guitar in your band?
questions.e: When who is the subject we usually do not use do / does: the verb takes -s (Who plays...?).

questions.q: Rita and Angela ___ work at the weekend.
questions.e: With a plural subject (they) the negative is don't + base verb.

questions.q: The human heart ___ blood around the body.
questions.e: Something that is always true → present simple. With it the verb takes -s: pumps.

questions.q: The train ___ at 7.45 tomorrow morning.
questions.e: We use the present simple for fixed timetables, even when they are in the future.

questions.s: She never plays football.
questions.fa: Say that she never plays football.
questions.e: Adverbs of frequency (never, always, sometimes) go before the main verb. With she the verb takes -s.

questions.s: Where do they work?
questions.fa: Ask where they work.
questions.e: Wh- question: question word + do / does + subject + base verb.

questions.s: John doesn't lives in Manchester.
questions.e: After doesn't the verb is in its base form, without -s.

questions.s: Does Rita usually gets up early?
questions.e: After Does the verb is in its base form, without -s.

questions.q: If it ___ (rain) tomorrow, we will get wet.
questions.e: After if we use the present simple, even when we talk about the future. With it the verb takes -s.

questions.q: More -ing forms
questions.e: Drop the final -e (have → having) or double the last letter after a short vowel (get → getting).

questions.q: Be quiet! The students ___ an exam.
questions.e: An action in progress right now → present continuous: are + V-ing.

questions.q: She ___ her friends tonight. They have arranged it.
questions.e: A future arrangement → present continuous.

questions.s: Is she cooking dinner?
questions.fa: Ask if she is cooking dinner.
questions.e: Question: am / is / are + subject + V-ing?

questions.s: The children are playing in the garden.
questions.fa: Say what the children are doing in the garden.
questions.e: Present continuous: are + V-ing.

questions.s: I am not feeling well today.
questions.fa: Say you are not feeling well.
questions.e: Negative: am not + V-ing.

questions.s: What is he eating?
questions.fa: Ask what he is eating.
questions.e: Question: Wh- word + is + subject + V-ing?

questions.s: My parents are staying at a hotel.
questions.fa: Say where your parents are staying.
questions.e: Temporary situation → present continuous.

questions.s: They are building a new school.
questions.fa: Say they are building a new school.
questions.e: Present continuous: are + V-ing.

questions.s: She are dancing now.
questions.e: With she we use is.

questions.s: I am not listen to you.
questions.e: After am not the verb takes -ing.

questions.s: Is they sleeping now?
questions.e: With they the question starts with Are.

questions.s: The cat is sleep on the sofa.
questions.e: After is the verb takes -ing.

questions.s: We are study English now.
questions.e: After are the verb takes -ing.

questions.s: Where is you going?
questions.e: With you we use are.

questions.q: My mother ___ (cook) dinner right now.
questions.e: right now → present continuous: is + V-ing.

questions.q: We ___ (not / watch) TV at the moment.
questions.e: Negative: are not + V-ing.

questions.q: The birds ___ (sing) in the trees.
questions.e: An action in progress now → are + V-ing.

questions.q: I ___ (wait) for the bus now.
questions.e: With I the auxiliary is am.

questions.q: She ___ (write) an email at the moment.
questions.e: at the moment → present continuous.

questions.q: It ___ (not / rain) now.
questions.e: Negative: is not + V-ing.

questions.q: Please speak quietly. Dad ___ on the phone.
questions.e: An activity at the moment of speaking → present continuous: is + V-ing.

questions.q: ___ you listening to me?
questions.e: Present continuous questions put am / is / are before the subject.

questions.q: I ___ to Paris next Friday. I have already booked the ticket.
questions.e: A fixed arrangement for the future → present continuous.

questions.q: I ___ this song. It is my favourite.
questions.e: Stative verbs (love, like, know, want) are not normally used in the continuous.

questions.s: He is not working today.
questions.fa: Say he is not working today.
questions.e: Negative: am / is / are + not + V-ing.

questions.s: Where are you going?
questions.fa: Ask where someone is going.
questions.e: Question: question word + am / is / are + subject + V-ing.

questions.s: They are watch TV now.
questions.e: After am / is / are the verb takes -ing.

questions.s: We is having lunch now.
questions.e: With we we use are: We are having lunch.

questions.q: At the moment, I ___ (read) a very good book.
questions.e: Something temporary happening around now → am + V-ing.

questions.q: Look! It ___ (snow).
questions.e: Look! shows something happening right now → is + V-ing.

questions.q: Look! The baby ___ now.
questions.e: Look and now show that the action is happening right now → present continuous: am / is / are + V-ing.

questions.q: They ___ football at the moment.
questions.e: at the moment → present continuous. With they we use are + V-ing.

questions.q: I ___ to music right now.
questions.e: With I the auxiliary is am: I am listening.

questions.q: What ___ you doing?
questions.e: Present continuous question: Wh- word + am / is / are + subject + V-ing.

questions.s: She is reading a book now.
questions.fa: Something is happening right now.
questions.e: Present continuous: subject + am / is / are + V-ing.

questions.s: We are not watching TV.
questions.fa: Say you are not watching TV at the moment.
questions.e: Negative: am / is / are + not + V-ing.

questions.s: They is playing football now.
questions.e: With They we must use are: They are playing.

questions.s: I am play a game now.
questions.e: After am / is / are the verb takes -ing.

questions.q: Listen! Someone ___ (knock) at the door.
questions.e: Listen! means right now → present continuous: is + V-ing.

questions.q: The children ___ (run) in the garden now.
questions.e: run → running (the last letter doubles).

questions.q: Adding -ing
questions.e: Drop the final -e (make → making) or double the last letter after a short vowel (run → running).

questions.q: He ___ breakfast at seven this morning.
questions.e: The past of have is had.

questions.q: My parents ___ married in 1998.
questions.e: The past of be with a plural subject is were.

questions.s: She wrote a letter to her friend.
questions.fa: Say what she wrote.
questions.e: write is irregular: the past is wrote.

questions.s: We watched a film last night.
questions.fa: Say what you watched last night.
questions.e: Regular past simple: verb + -ed.

questions.s: Did he finish the work?
questions.fa: Ask if he finished the work.
questions.e: After Did the verb stays in the base form.

questions.s: I did not hear the phone.
questions.fa: Say you did not hear the phone.
questions.e: Negative past: did not + base verb.

questions.s: They arrived at the hotel late.
questions.fa: Say they arrived late at the hotel.
questions.e: Regular past simple: arrive + d.

questions.s: Why did you leave early?
questions.fa: Ask why someone left early.
questions.e: Question: question word + did + subject + base verb.

questions.s: I seen him yesterday.
questions.e: The past simple of see is saw. seen is the past participle.

questions.s: She didn't went to school.
questions.e: After didn't the verb is in its base form.

questions.s: They play football last Sunday.
questions.e: last Sunday → past simple: played.

questions.s: Where did you stayed?
questions.e: After did the verb stays in its base form.

questions.s: He taked my bag.
questions.e: take is irregular: the past is took.

questions.s: We was at home yesterday.
questions.e: With we the past of be is were.

questions.q: She ___ (write) a long email yesterday.
questions.e: write is irregular: the past is wrote.

questions.q: We ___ (go) to the beach last summer.
questions.e: The past of go is went.

questions.q: I ___ (visit) my uncle two days ago.
questions.e: Regular past simple: visit + ed.

questions.q: ___ (do) you finish your homework?
questions.e: Past simple questions start with Did.

questions.q: They ___ (not / come) to school on Monday.
questions.e: Negative past: didn't + base verb.

questions.q: He ___ (buy) a new bike last month.
questions.e: The past of buy is bought.

questions.q: I met my best friend two years ___.
questions.e: ago comes after a period of time and is used with the past simple: two years ago.

questions.q: Where ___ you buy that jacket?
questions.e: Past simple questions use did + subject + base verb.

questions.q: Who ___ the window yesterday?
questions.e: When who is the subject of the question we do not use did: Who broke the window?

questions.q: We ___ get home until midnight.
questions.e: Negative past: didn't + base verb.

questions.s: They did not enjoy the film.
questions.fa: Say they did not enjoy the film.
questions.e: Negative past: did not + base verb.

questions.s: When did you move to this city?
questions.fa: Ask when someone moved to this city.
questions.e: Past simple question: question word + did + subject + base verb.

questions.s: He buyed a new phone last week.
questions.e: buy is irregular and its past is bought.

questions.s: Did she called you last night?
questions.e: After Did the verb stays in its base form.

questions.q: My grandparents ___ (live) in Spain for ten years.
questions.e: Something that was true for some time in the past → past simple.

questions.q: I ___ (not / see) you at the party yesterday.
questions.e: Negative past: didn't + base verb.

questions.q: Yesterday we ___ to the zoo.
questions.e: yesterday means past simple; the past of go is went (irregular).

questions.q: I ___ my homework last night.
questions.e: last night → past; the past of do is did.

questions.q: She didn't ___ the answer.
questions.e: After didn't the verb is always in its base form (no -s, no -ed).

questions.q: ___ you see Ali yesterday?
questions.e: Past simple questions start with Did.

questions.s: I visited my grandmother last week.
questions.fa: Say what you did last week.
questions.e: Past simple with a regular verb: verb + -ed.

questions.s: They did not go to school yesterday.
questions.fa: Say they did NOT go to school yesterday.
questions.e: Negative past: did not + base verb.

questions.s: She goed to the market.
questions.e: go is irregular and its past is went, not goed.

questions.s: Did you went there?
questions.e: After Did the verb stays in its base form: Did you go there?

questions.q: We ___ (eat) pizza last Friday.
questions.e: The past of eat is ate.

questions.q: He ___ (not / like) the movie yesterday.
questions.e: Negative past: didn't + base verb.

questions.q: Irregular verbs — 1
questions.e: The past forms of these verbs are irregular and must be memorised.

questions.q: Irregular verbs — 2
questions.e: The past forms of these verbs are irregular and must be memorised.

questions.q: Spelling: more -ing forms
questions.e: Drop the final -e, double the last letter, or change -ie to -ying.

questions.q: The children ___ in the park when it began to rain.
questions.e: An action in progress when something happened → were + V-ing.

questions.q: ___ it raining when you left home?
questions.e: With it the past continuous uses was. Questions start with Was / Were.

questions.s: She was cooking dinner at six.
questions.fa: Say what she was doing at six.
questions.e: Past continuous: was + V-ing.

questions.s: Were they sleeping at midnight?
questions.fa: Ask if they were sleeping at midnight.
questions.e: Question: Was / Were + subject + V-ing?

questions.s: I was not paying attention.
questions.fa: Say you were not paying attention.
questions.e: Negative: was not + V-ing.

questions.s: The phone rang while we were eating.
questions.fa: Say the phone rang during your meal.
questions.e: while + past continuous: the longer action in progress.

questions.s: He was waiting for the bus.
questions.fa: Say he was waiting for the bus.
questions.e: Past continuous: was + V-ing.

questions.s: We were playing outside all afternoon.
questions.fa: Say you were playing outside the whole afternoon.
questions.e: The past continuous can show an activity in progress for some time.

questions.s: I were studying at eight.
questions.e: With I the past of be is was.

questions.s: She was cook when I arrived.
questions.e: After was / were the verb takes -ing.

questions.s: Was you watching TV?
questions.e: With you we use were.

questions.s: They wasn't listening.
questions.e: With they we use were.

questions.s: He was sleep while I was working.
questions.e: After was the verb takes -ing.

questions.s: We were play football at five.
questions.e: After were the verb takes -ing.

questions.q: I ___ (sleep) when the alarm rang.
questions.e: An action in progress when another action happened → was + V-ing.

questions.q: They ___ (walk) home when it started to rain.
questions.e: With they we use were + V-ing.

questions.q: She ___ (not / listen) to the teacher.
questions.e: Negative: wasn't + V-ing.

questions.q: ___ (be) you studying at 10 pm?
questions.e: With you the past continuous uses Were.

questions.q: My dad ___ (drive) to work when he saw an accident.
questions.e: Longer action → past continuous; the short action (saw) → past simple.

questions.q: We ___ (have) dinner when the guests arrived.
questions.e: An action in progress when another action happened → were + V-ing.

questions.q: What ___ you doing at half past six yesterday?
questions.e: With you the past continuous uses were: What were you doing...?

questions.q: My sister ___ a video when the internet stopped.
questions.e: A longer action in progress (past continuous) is interrupted by a shorter action (past simple).

questions.q: I cut my finger while I ___ vegetables.
questions.e: while + past continuous: the chopping was in progress when the accident happened.

questions.q: I called Tom, but he didn't answer. He ___ a shower.
questions.e: An action that was in progress at that moment → was + V-ing.

questions.s: What were you doing at nine?
questions.fa: Ask what someone was doing at nine.
questions.e: Question: What + was / were + subject + V-ing?

questions.s: It was raining when we left.
questions.fa: Say what the weather was doing when you left.
questions.e: Past continuous for the background action, past simple for the short action.

questions.s: I was walk to school when it started to rain.
questions.e: After was / were the verb takes -ing.

questions.s: They was watching a film at ten.
questions.e: With they we use were, not was.

questions.q: We ___ (play) cards when the lights went out.
questions.e: An action in progress that was interrupted → were + V-ing.

questions.q: It ___ (not / snow) when I looked outside.
questions.e: Negative: wasn't + V-ing.

questions.q: I ___ TV when you called.
questions.e: An action in progress at a moment in the past → was / were + V-ing. With I we use was.

questions.q: They ___ football at five o'clock yesterday.
questions.e: A specific time in the past → past continuous. With they we use were.

questions.q: While she ___, the phone rang.
questions.e: while + past continuous shows the longer action that was in progress.

questions.q: ___ you sleeping when I came home?
questions.e: With you the past continuous uses were.

questions.s: I was reading a book at eight.
questions.fa: Say what you were doing at eight.
questions.e: Past continuous: subject + was / were + V-ing.

questions.s: They were not listening to the teacher.
questions.fa: Say they were not listening to the teacher.
questions.e: Negative: was / were + not + V-ing.

questions.s: She were sleeping when I called.
questions.e: With she / he / it / I we use was, not were.

questions.s: We was walking in the park.
questions.e: With we / you / they we use were, not was.

questions.q: He ___ (study) when the light went out.
questions.e: An action in progress when another action interrupted → was + V-ing.

questions.q: My parents ___ (not / watch) TV at that time.
questions.e: Negative: weren't + V-ing.

questions.q: Adding -ing (spelling)
questions.e: Words ending in -ie change to -ying; short-vowel words double the last letter; words ending in -e drop the e.

questions.q: She ___ in Tehran for ten years.
questions.e: for + a period of time up to now → present perfect.

questions.q: I haven't seen him ___ Monday.
questions.e: since + a point in time (Monday) → present perfect.

questions.s: She has just finished her homework.
questions.fa: Say she finished her homework a moment ago.
questions.e: just goes between has / have and the past participle.

questions.s: Has he ever visited London?
questions.fa: Ask if he has ever visited London.
questions.e: Question: Has / Have + subject + ever + past participle?

questions.s: They have lived in Shiraz since 2015.
questions.fa: Say since when they have lived in Shiraz.
questions.e: since + a point in time → present perfect.

questions.s: I have not finished my work yet.
questions.fa: Say you have not finished your work.
questions.e: yet is used with negatives in the present perfect.

questions.s: We have known each other for years.
questions.fa: Say you have known each other for a long time.
questions.e: for + a period of time → present perfect.

questions.s: How long have you studied English?
questions.fa: Ask how long someone has studied English.
questions.e: How long + have / has + subject + past participle?

questions.s: She have been to Italy twice.
questions.e: With she we use has.

questions.s: I have eat lunch already.
questions.e: After have we use the past participle: eaten.

questions.s: Have you ever see a whale?
questions.e: After have we use the past participle: seen.

questions.s: He has lived here since three years.
questions.e: for + a period of time (three years); since + a point in time.

questions.s: They has just arrived.
questions.e: With they we use have.

questions.s: We haven't finish yet.
questions.e: After haven't we use the past participle: finished.

questions.q: She has ___ (finish) her homework.
questions.e: Past participle of a regular verb: finish + ed.

questions.q: We have ___ (be) friends since 2010.
questions.e: The past participle of be is been.

questions.q: He has ___ (break) his phone.
questions.e: The past participle of break is broken.

questions.q: I ___ (live) here for two years.
questions.e: for + a period of time → present perfect.

questions.q: They ___ (not / see) this film yet.
questions.e: Negative present perfect: haven't + past participle.

questions.q: She has ___ (take) three photos today.
questions.e: The past participle of take is taken.

questions.q: I ___ my keys, so I can't open the door.
questions.e: A past action with a result in the present (no keys now) → present perfect.

questions.q: Have you finished your homework ___?
questions.e: yet is used in questions and negatives with the present perfect.

questions.q: We ___ in this house since 2018.
questions.e: since + a starting point in time → present perfect.

questions.q: I ___ Paris in 2019.
questions.e: With a finished time (in 2019) we use the past simple, not the present perfect.

questions.s: Have you ever eaten Persian food?
questions.fa: Ask if someone has ever eaten Persian food.
questions.e: Experience: Have + subject + ever + past participle?

questions.s: We have not seen him today.
questions.fa: Say you have not seen him today.
questions.e: today is an unfinished time → present perfect: have not + past participle.

questions.s: I have went to the shop this morning.
questions.e: The past participle of go is gone; went is the past simple.

questions.s: She has live here since 2015.
questions.e: After has / have we need the past participle: lived.

questions.q: I have never ___ (see) snow.
questions.e: never + have + past participle: seen.

questions.q: They ___ (just / arrive) at the station.
questions.e: just goes between have and the past participle.

questions.q: I ___ already finished my homework.
questions.e: With I we use have: I have finished.

questions.q: She has ___ to Paris twice.
questions.e: have / has + past participle. The past participle of be is been.

questions.q: We ___ lived here since 2020.
questions.e: since + a point in time → present perfect; with we the auxiliary is have.

questions.q: ___ you ever eaten sushi?
questions.e: Present perfect questions start with Have / Has: Have you ever...?

questions.s: I have never seen a tiger.
questions.fa: Say you have never seen a tiger.
questions.e: have + never + past participle (seen).

questions.s: She has lived here for five years.
questions.fa: Say how long she has lived here.
questions.e: for + a period of time → present perfect.

questions.s: He have finished his work.
questions.e: With He (third person singular) we need has.

questions.s: I have saw that film.
questions.e: After have we use the past participle: seen, not saw.

questions.q: They have just ___ (arrive) at the airport.
questions.e: Past participle of a regular verb: arrive + d → arrived.

questions.q: She has ___ (write) three letters.
questions.e: The past participle of write is written.

questions.q: Past participles — 1
questions.e: Irregular past participles must be memorised.

questions.q: Past participles — 2
questions.e: Irregular past participles must be memorised.

questions.q: Short forms of will (more)
questions.e: In speaking we usually use the short forms.

questions.q: I'm hungry. I ___ make a sandwich.
questions.e: A spontaneous decision at the moment of speaking → will.

questions.q: We ___ be late. I promise.
questions.e: A promise about the future: won't (will not) + base verb.

questions.s: I will help you with the bags.
questions.fa: Offer to help with the bags.
questions.e: An offer → will + base verb.

questions.s: She will not forget your birthday.
questions.fa: Promise that she will not forget your birthday.
questions.e: Negative: will not + base verb.

questions.s: Will you open the door, please?
questions.fa: Ask someone politely to open the door.
questions.e: A request: Will you + base verb...?

questions.s: I think it will be cold tomorrow.
questions.fa: Say what you think about tomorrow's weather.
questions.e: An opinion about the future → will + base verb.

questions.s: They will win the game, I think.
questions.fa: Say you think they will win the game.
questions.e: A prediction → will + base verb.

questions.s: Wait here until I come back.
questions.fa: Tell someone to wait until you come back.
questions.e: After until we use the present simple for the future.

questions.s: It will raining tomorrow.
questions.e: After will the verb is in its base form.

questions.s: Will she comes to the party?
questions.e: After Will + subject the verb is in its base form.

questions.s: I will not to tell anyone.
questions.e: After will not the base verb follows directly, without to.

questions.s: He won't goes with us.
questions.e: After won't the verb is in its base form.

questions.s: I'll call you when I will arrive.
questions.e: After when we use the present simple for the future.

questions.s: We will meeting him tomorrow.
questions.e: After will the verb is in its base form.

questions.q: Don't worry. She ___ (be) fine.
questions.e: A belief about the future → will + base verb.

questions.q: I ___ (not / tell) anyone your secret.
questions.e: A promise → will. Negative: won't + base verb.

questions.q: ___ (will) you open the window, please?
questions.e: Requests can start with Will you...?

questions.q: I think they ___ (win) the match.
questions.e: An opinion about the future → will + base verb.

questions.q: I ___ (call) you when I get home.
questions.e: A promise → will + base verb.

questions.q: We ___ (be) late if we don't hurry.
questions.e: First conditional result: will + base verb.

questions.q: I'm sure Sara ___ love the gift.
questions.e: A belief about the future (I'm sure) → will + base verb.

questions.q: The phone is ringing. I ___ answer it.
questions.e: A spontaneous decision at the moment of speaking → will.

questions.q: ___ you help me with my bag, please?
questions.e: Will you...? is a common way to make a request.

questions.q: I will call you when I ___ home.
questions.e: After when / until / after we use the present simple for the future, not will.

questions.s: Will it rain tomorrow?
questions.fa: Ask if you think it will rain tomorrow.
questions.e: Question with will: Will + subject + base verb?

questions.s: We will not be late.
questions.fa: Promise that you will not be late.
questions.e: Negative: will not + base verb.

questions.s: She will arrives at six.
questions.e: After will the verb is in its base form, without -s.

questions.s: I will phone you when I will get home.
questions.e: After when we use the present simple for the future: when I get home.

questions.q: Don't worry. I ___ (carry) the bag for you.
questions.e: An offer made at the moment of speaking → will.

questions.q: My team ___ (win) the match, I think.
questions.e: An opinion about the future (I think) → will + base verb.

questions.q: I think she ___ pass the exam.
questions.e: An opinion or prediction after I think → will + base verb.

questions.q: I'm cold. I ___ close the window.
questions.e: A decision made at the moment of speaking → will.

questions.q: Don't worry. I ___ help you.
questions.e: A promise or an offer to help → will.

questions.q: She is ill. She ___ come to the party.
questions.e: won't = will not. Use will not + base verb for a negative future.

questions.s: I will call you tomorrow.
questions.fa: Promise to phone someone tomorrow.
questions.e: will + base verb (no to).

questions.s: He will not be late.
questions.fa: Say he will not be late.
questions.e: Negative: will not + base verb.

questions.s: He will goes to school tomorrow.
questions.e: After will the verb is in its base form, with no -s.

questions.s: She will to help us.
questions.e: After will we use the base verb directly, without to.

questions.q: Tomorrow it ___ (be) sunny. I think so.
questions.e: An opinion or prediction → will + be.

questions.q: I ___ (not / forget) your birthday. I promise.
questions.e: A promise → will. Negative: won't + base verb.

questions.q: Short forms of will
questions.e: In speaking we usually use the short forms.

questions.q: We have booked the tickets. We ___ fly to Dubai next week.
questions.e: A plan that is already decided → be going to.

questions.q: Look at his face! He ___ cry.
questions.e: We can see signs that it will happen → be going to.

questions.s: I am going to visit my grandparents.
questions.fa: Say you plan to visit your grandparents.
questions.e: A plan → am / is / are + going to + base verb.

questions.s: What are you going to do tonight?
questions.fa: Ask about someone's plan for tonight.
questions.e: Question: Wh- word + are + subject + going to + base verb?

questions.s: He is going to be a doctor.
questions.fa: Say he plans to become a doctor.
questions.e: A plan → is going to + base verb.

questions.s: We are not going to travel this summer.
questions.fa: Say you have no plan to travel this summer.
questions.e: Negative: are not going to + base verb.

questions.s: Is she going to cook dinner?
questions.fa: Ask if she plans to cook dinner.
questions.e: Question: Is + subject + going to + base verb?

questions.s: It is going to snow tonight.
questions.fa: Say it is going to snow tonight because you can see the signs.
questions.e: A prediction based on evidence → be going to.

questions.s: I am going to buys a car.
questions.e: After going to the verb is in its base form.

questions.s: He are going to call you.
questions.e: With he we use is.

questions.s: We is going to play tennis.
questions.e: With we we use are.

questions.s: They are going to watching a film.
questions.e: After going to the verb is in its base form.

questions.s: Are you going to cooks tonight?
questions.e: After going to the verb is in its base form.

questions.s: My brother am going to study law.
questions.e: With my brother (he) we use is.

questions.q: We ___ (have) a picnic on Saturday. I have made sandwiches.
questions.e: A plan already made → are going to + base verb.

questions.q: She ___ (study) medicine. It is her plan.
questions.e: A plan → is going to + base verb.

questions.q: Look at the sky! It ___ (rain).
questions.e: A prediction from evidence we can see → is going to.

questions.q: I ___ (not / watch) TV tonight. I have homework.
questions.e: Negative with I: am not going to + base verb.

questions.q: ___ (be) you going to join us?
questions.e: With you the question starts with Are.

questions.q: He ___ (not / buy) that car. It is too expensive.
questions.e: Negative: is not going to + base verb.

questions.q: Watch out! That glass ___ fall off the table.
questions.e: We can see that it will happen (evidence) → be going to.

questions.q: I have decided: I ___ learn the guitar this year.
questions.e: A decision made before speaking → be going to.

questions.q: Where ___ they going to stay in London?
questions.e: Question: Wh- word + are + they + going to + base verb.

questions.q: My sister ___ going to move to Canada next year.
questions.e: With she (third person singular) the auxiliary is is.

questions.s: Are you going to wear a coat?
questions.fa: Ask if someone plans to wear a coat.
questions.e: Question: am / is / are + subject + going to + base verb?

questions.s: He is not going to study tonight.
questions.fa: Say he has no plan to study tonight.
questions.e: Negative: is not going to + base verb.

questions.s: We are going to played football.
questions.e: After going to the verb is in its base form: going to play.

questions.s: She are going to buy a car.
questions.e: With she we use is: She is going to buy.

questions.q: I ___ (paint) my room this weekend. I have the paint.
questions.e: A plan made before speaking → am going to + base verb.

questions.q: They ___ (not / go) on holiday this summer.
questions.e: Negative: are not going to + base verb.

questions.q: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
questions.e: A prediction based on evidence we can see (the clouds) → be going to.

questions.q: We ___ visit Shiraz next month. We have bought the tickets.
questions.e: A plan that was already decided → be going to.

questions.q: What ___ you going to do this weekend?
questions.e: Question: Wh- word + am / is / are + subject + going to + base verb.

questions.q: I ___ going to study tonight.
questions.e: With I the auxiliary is am: I am going to study.

questions.s: She is going to buy a new bag.
questions.fa: Say she plans to buy a new bag.
questions.e: Structure: am / is / are + going to + base verb.

questions.s: They are not going to play today.
questions.fa: Say they have no plan to play today.
questions.e: Negative: am / is / are + not + going to + base verb.

questions.s: I am going to meets him.
questions.e: After going to the verb is in its base form: going to meet.

questions.s: They is going to travel by train.
questions.e: With They we must use are: They are going to travel.

questions.q: I ___ (visit) my aunt tonight. I have a plan.
questions.e: A plan made before → am going to + base verb.

questions.q: My parents ___ (buy) a new car next week.
questions.e: A plan for the future with they → are going to + base verb.

questions.q: More short forms of be going to
questions.e: In speaking we usually use the short forms.

questions.q: Short forms of be going to
questions.e: In speaking we usually use the short forms.
